history.summary: Ancient temple of Goddess Chandi, the presiding deity of Cuttack, near the banks of the Mahanadi at Chandni Chowk/Buxi Bazar. Legend: Chandi was the deity of the medieval Gajapati rulers; when invaders came, the idol was buried. Centuries later Hansa Panda, purohit of the Kanika king, dreamed the Goddess asking to be unearthed; diggers found ~40 bullock-cart loads of red sindoor and the four-armed idol (noose, goad, abhaya, varada). The fifth generation of the founder priest's family still performs the daily rituals. Locals revere her as the 'Living Goddess of Cuttack'. Durga Puja here runs 16 days with the goddess adorned in many beshas (Suna Besha, Ugratara, Hari Chandi, Mahishasuramardini, etc.). Attracts over 20 lakh devotees a year. Note: only Hindus are allowed inside per the Odisha Hindu Religious Endowments listing.

name: Cuttack Chandi Temple
town_description: Cuttack, the 'Silver City' and 'Millennium City' of Odisha, was the state's capital for nearly a thousand years and sits at the head of the Mahanadi delta. It is famed for filigree silverwork (tarakasi), the 14th-century Barabati Fort, and a dense tradition of Durga Puja celebrations. A major commercial and cultural centre, it is the headquarters of Cuttack district.
